author: Rinehart
text:
Looking at some of my recent trades which failed, I've noticed I'm falling for a similar trick over and over...

A mistake I've been making regularly is setting up trade plans but not
considering when there is a zone of liquidity right past my stop loss. I
 think this is probably going back to overconfidence and some
overtrading. I've been so bloody excited to finally have something
profitable with a high win rate, I've been trying to be part of every
trade on every pair. I've been taking trades that have PA and LS lining
 up with clean orders, but often I've been ignoring the need for there
to be a trick. The need for a BSZ, DM, compression on approach, or a
FO, etc.

Every trade doesn't have to have a trick of course. However, most of
the really good trades do. Most of my trades are entered overnight
while I'm asleep during the EUR session. I don't have the benefit of
watching the approach on LTF most times due to work. Emotionally this
is good, lol. But it is bad if I'm trying to trade these trades that
lack a trick. Moving forward I'm going to work harder on thinking like
Staurum....if this trade doesn't play out like I expect, what are other
likely scenarios?

I used to have a saying before I found RTM. I would say, "It is best to
 wait for someone to get F___ed before entering a trade." At the time I
 didn't realize how right I was! Now that I've joined RTM, I'm trying
to enter while they are getting screwed instead of after, lol.

author: Astrokillah
text:
Thanks Rinehart, please never ever apologize!!

Your chart has shown that I still have a hell lot to learn, because I am
 missing some important FLs on my chart! And there is also problem
associated with scale.

I actually took a touch trade at location 1, which I initially thought
was the MPL of FL-B. It was a winner but that's beside the point.

The thing is, I didn't realize that FL-D exists! Because if I knew that
FL-D existed, I would not have taken a TT as I would be worried about a
FO to FL-D.

In terms of scale, FL-A and FL-B (green) are FLs that are visible on H1
and H4 timeframes. Whereas FL-C and FL-D (purple) are visible on M30 and
 below.

This brings a lot of dilemma, with so many FLs (big and small), I see
too many places where price could bounce or FO to. It's very difficult
to find the space to trade.

As I embarked on learning how to draw FL, I was hoping that I could
figure out a mechanical way to draw FL that would make it easier to
analyze order flow, to help us understand the hidden agenda of ITs. But
as you can see, in this example, we have H1's FL stacked on top of M30's
 FL. And on the above chart, even if I don't draw it, I can already see
that if we go down another TF, we can draw another FL that's stacked
immediately underneath FL-D! So.. it's nightmare!

author: Rinehart
text:
In nature we see lovely examples of fractals. We can see a plant or
shell that looks the same on smaller scales as it does on bigger scales.
 The market is structured the same way. The smaller pieces combine to
form the bigger pieces.

author: Rinehart
text:
When we trade, we are interested in trading around HTF boundaries but on LTF.
 A FL on Weekly will contain at least 2 or 3 FLs on 4hr. It will
contain many more on a 1 minute chart. However, only a few of those 1
or 5 min FLs would be near the HTF boundary, have fresh orders, proper
LS, etc. It is our job to identify which one(s) to trade after we get
an engulf.

author: Rinehart
text:
I used Weekly, 4hr and 15 min charts to breakdown important areas. If
 I wanted to go to even smaller time frames, I would probably use 4hr,
15 min and 1 min. I'm sure it is possible to go from Monthly to 1min.
But your charts would be unreadable.

I haven't talked about Eng in these charts because I wanted to impress
on you the importance of playing "important FLs." The ones around the
boundaries. It is our job to find the good ones. We also of course
need PA to tell us where ITs want to go.

Now to think a little bit about Eng. If we have an Eng of of a 1 min FL
 without engulfing any HTF FLs. Well, that is PA and we can expect
price to reach the next 1 min FL before breaking the FL behind us. You
can play it and place targets based on the 1 min chart. On the other
hand, if you have an engulf on daily chart, then you can use daily
targets. Now think about the video IF made showing GBPUSD Daily. The
QM video where he showed a 50R trade. This was a LS kink QM trade. Now
 imagine that you dropped from daily down to 15 min to sharpen your SL.
 It is as simple as that.

author: Rinehart
text:
Canceling new sell limit on USDCHF. The trade is still viable but
late in the day on Friday is dangerous. Liquidity Providers widen
spreads to stop out suckers. My observation is that normally they widen
 the ASK line (on top) and leave the bid line. Above the ask is where
my SL resides so I'll avoid the danger.

Why the ask line? Because our charts are setup to print candles from
the Bid prices. Therefore they can hit the our stops at end of the day
rollover or end of week without leaving a printed record of their
manipulation.
